newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr holds on to small gains above 126 yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr holds on to small gains above 126 yen in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar held on to small gains above 126 yen in late Tokyo on Thursday due to buying by U.S. securities houses and Japanese importers, dealers said.

But it was inhibited from further rises due to hedge sales by Japanese investors and exporters' sales above 126.30 yen amid growing caution ahead of Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) nations' meeting in Washington, they added.

Views among operators were divided ahead of the G7 meeting, with Japanese importers who have failed to buy sufficient dollars lifting their bids due to fears that the outcome of the meeting may not hurt dollar sentiment.

Meanwhile, Japanese life insurers, trust banks and exporters were intent on selling dollars on rises, notably above 126.50 yen, due to risks of dollar-selling intervention after the end of the G7 meeting.
"Views on the dollar's direction were mixed, which kept trading within a narrow range," said a senior dealer at a European bank.
